title: thread.yml — the thread's metadata
$comment: What the thread is, edited by hand by people and agents; the tool writes it on create, reanchor (title) and reparent (parent). It is validated on every read. What happened lives in log.jsonl, and the thread's state (lifecycle, claims, counts, children, links) is computed from the log on read and never stored. Namespace is the folder. A thread.yml carrying state, tip or children is the older cache format; `thread migrate` turns it into this file. The same shape is recorded in each checkpoint's `metadata` block and in the `migrated` event, as the baseline for the view's 'thread.yml since the last checkpoint' line.

title.description: Human title, one line. The folder's slug was derived from the first title and doesn't follow later changes.

parent.description: Set on subthreads. Blank or absent means top-level. Never the thread's own id (a validation error). A parent id that matches no thread, names a thread in another namespace, or leads back to this thread is a doctor finding; the thread reads as top-level meanwhile. An unquoted all-digit id, which YAML reads as a number, is read as the id.

anyOf.description: an unquoted all-digit id, read as the id

from-task.description: Set by `thread promote`: the task on the parent's board this thread came from.

supersedes.description: Legacy pointer from the retired supersede command. Kept for old threads only; don't add it to new ones.

anyOf.description: an unquoted all-digit id, read as the id

flags.description: Free-form: your own keys, each with a single value. Prefix keys with your tool's name (kiln.autonomous); not enforced. The view shows them on one line and counts changes to them.
